title: Module 5 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: The distribution of sample means is
o: The distribution of means from all possible samples of a given size
The distribution of scores in one sample
items.why: It is a theoretical distribution. Each point is a sample mean, not a person.

items.q: The standard error of the mean is
o: The standard deviation of the distribution of sample means
The standard deviation of the population
items.why: It measures how much sample means typically differ from the population mean.

items.q: The standard error is computed as
o: Population SD divided by the square root of n
Population SD times the square root of n
items.why: SE = sigma divided by square root of n. Larger samples give smaller standard errors.

items.q: The central limit theorem says that the distribution of sample means
o: Approaches a normal shape as n increases, whatever the population shape
Has a mean equal to zero
items.why: With n of about 30 or more, the distribution of means is close to normal even for skewed populations.

items.q: The mean of the distribution of sample means equals
o: The sample mean of one sample
items.why: Sample means are unbiased. They center on the population mean.

items.q: If you quadruple the sample size, the standard error
items.why: The square root of 4 is 2, so SE is divided by 2.

items.q: Which is true of a larger sample compared with a smaller one drawn from the same population?
o: Its mean is likely closer to the population mean
Its mean is always exactly the population mean
items.why: Larger samples have smaller standard errors, so their means tend to land closer to the parameter.

items.q: A z score for a sample mean is computed as
o: (M minus mu) divided by the standard error
items.why: The standard error replaces the standard deviation because we are locating a mean in the distribution of means.

o: The natural difference between a sample statistic and its parameter
A mistake made by the researcher
The same as a sample SD
items.why: It is unavoidable but measurable, and the standard error quantifies it.

items.q: The distribution of sample means is less variable than the population because
o: Averaging cancels out some extreme scores
items.why: Extreme high and low scores offset one another within a sample mean.
